title: TL/UL equivalence + rigid rotation tests
objective: End-to-end verification that the UL path is numerically consistent: on a cantilever beam benchmark, TL and UL must produce identical converged displacements within 1e-8; on a rigid rotation test, the Cauchy stress rate must be zero to machine precision under all three objective rates.

plan_assets.asset_description: B1 exit criterion — UL solver produces identical results to TL on shared benchmarks, objective rates verified via rigid rotation test.

scope: Add a handwritten UL reference solver under `tests/ref/ref_hex8_ul.py` mirroring `ref_hex8_elastic.py` but with the UL residual and tangent.
Parametrize an existing cantilever benchmark (or add a dedicated one) so it runs both TL and UL and asserts |u_TL - u_UL| < 1e-8.
Add a rigid-rotation regression test: apply a 30-degree rotation, assert the Cauchy stress rate vanishes to 1e-12 under Jaumann (and 1e-10 under the others).
implementation_steps: Copy `ref_hex8_elastic.py` to `ref_hex8_ul.py` and replace the TL residual/tangent with their UL counterparts.
Add `test_ul_equivalence.py` under `tests/` with TL-vs-UL cantilever and rigid rotation tests.
Mark the TL-vs-UL test as `@pytest.mark.slow` (Newton solve on a 4x4x4 cantilever takes O(1s)).
Add a FAST unit test covering the rigid-rotation stress-rate invariant.
acceptance_criteria: TL and UL converged displacements agree within 1e-8 on the cantilever test (slow).
Rigid-rotation Cauchy-rate test passes for all three objective rates (fast).
Both tests are marked correctly (slow vs fast) and collected by pytest.
risks: The cantilever test may not converge under UL if the Newton preconditioner / step size is wrong. Mitigation: start from the known-converged TL displacement as an initial guess for UL.
Numerical noise near machine epsilon can make the 1e-8 tolerance too tight. Mitigation: loosen to 1e-6 if needed and document in the test docstring.

commands.command: uv run pytest packages/mechdsl-core/tests/ -m 'not slow and not gpu' -q

completion_notes: Handwritten UL reference solver (ref_hex8_ul.py) with Truesdell tangent + standard geometric stiffness. 4x2x1 cantilever: TL/UL displacements agree within 1e-8. Rigid rotation: all three objective rates vanish to 1e-12 (Jaumann) / 1e-10 (Truesdell, GN). Resolved P1-4 deferred tangent FD stub. Phase 1 exit criterion met — zero remaining skips.
